etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English ymagynatif, from Middle French imaginatif, from Medieval Latin imāginātīvus.

definitions.definition: Having a lively or creative imagination.

quote.citation: 1951 December, Helen Weissenstein, “Readers' Forum”, in Chess Review:
quote.text: No doubt kibitzers are highly imaginative. How else could they see wins and brilliant combinations that do not exist?

definitions.definition: Tending to be fanciful or inventive.
